record.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:~1063-1073 — members' destination calendars silently dropped when the organizer has none: the ternary yields `null` making the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` a no-op, inconsistent with other call sites that fall back to `[]`

adjudication.rationale:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized with a ternary that falls back to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists:
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar
  ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar
  ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar]
  : null,
```
Later, for COLLECTIVE team events, member calendars are appended via optional chaining:
```ts
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
}
```
If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the `?.push(...)` is a no-op, so `teamDestinationCalendars` (collected from `users.slice(1)` when members have `user.destinationCalendar`) are silently dropped. This is inconsistent with many other updated call sites in the diff that default to `[]` (e.g., payments/webhooks/cancel/confirm handlers), and results in lost destination calendars in this edge case.
